memory_update.text: For the leading-edge foundry/equipment node, prioritize direct research on TSM, ASML, AMAT, LRCX, and KLAC before moving to second-order suppliers such as test, EDA/IP, materials, gases, and subsystems.
The node appears to split into at least four sub-chokepoints: advanced-node wafer capacity, EUV/High-NA lithography, etch/deposition/materials engineering, and process-control/yield management.

This pass did not include semiconductor test leaders such as Teradyne or Advantest, EDA/IP leaders such as Synopsys/Cadence/Arm, or materials/gases suppliers; those should be covered in a separate Layer 1B pass if the node is widened beyond foundry and core wafer-fab equipment.
Need a follow-up evidence pass focused on export-control exposure, China revenue concentration, backlog quality, shipment lead times, and capex-cycle timing for ASML, AMAT, LRCX, and KLAC.
ONTO should be tracked as a high-relevance process-control and advanced-packaging candidate for AI leading-edge/packaging bottlenecks; verify revenue mix and backlog quality.
MKSI adds subsystem breadth across vacuum, photonics, lasers and specialty chemicals; relevance is plausible but needs product-level mapping to leading-edge WFE and advanced packaging tools.
AEIS is a precision plasma-power supplier with explicit filing language tying 2025 semicap demand to AI-related leading-edge logic and memory; watch China/export-control and trailing-edge offsets.
UCTT and ICHR are subsystem/cleanliness/fluid-delivery names that may act as second-order WFE chokepoints but require stress tests for customer concentration, profitability and cyclicality.

This pass did not include OTC/non-US primary listings such as Tokyo Electron or Advantest, nor EDA/IP names such as Synopsys, Cadence and Arm; those should be handled in separate passes if US-listed ADR/EDA/software exposure is in scope.
ONTO added as a focused metrology/inspection candidate for advanced packaging, HBM, hybrid bonding, and advanced-node process control linked to AI chip manufacturing.
CAMT added as a focused inspection/metrology candidate with explicit AI, HBM, and advanced-packaging demand exposure; validate customer concentration and platform adoption.
ENTG added as an underappreciated materials/purity/yield-enabler for advanced nodes, EUV, selective etch, deposition materials, CMP, filtration, and contamination control.
MKSI added as a second-order semiconductor equipment subsystem supplier with exposure to deposition/etch, process control, vacuum, and electronics/advanced packaging demand.
AMKR added as an adjacent advanced packaging/test capacity candidate, especially for U.S.-based packaging linked to TSMC Arizona and Apple supply-chain commitments.

For this node, the less-obvious chokepoint map should include not only foundries and primary WFE vendors, but also advanced packaging/test, metrology/inspection, high-purity materials, and WFE subsystem suppliers.
Still need a separate pass on EDA/IP and test vendors such as Synopsys, Cadence, Arm, Teradyne, and Advantest, plus specialized gases/chemicals where US-listed exposure may be indirect.

node: Leading-edge foundry capacity and semiconductor equipment
summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Expanded the US-listed universe for the leading-edge foundry and semiconductor equipment node. The highest-direct-exposure candidates are TSMC as the leading advanced-node foundry/advanced-packaging asset owner, ASML as the EUV lithography chokepoint, and Applied Materials, Lam Research, and KLA as major wafer-fab equipment and process-control suppliers tied to leading-edge logic, DRAM/HBM, advanced packaging, and yield learning. This is a research universe only, not a buy/sell list. This pass expands the US-listed universe beyond the obvious foundry and wafer-fab-equipment leaders into second-order but potentially chokepoint-relevant suppliers: process control/advanced packaging inspection, vacuum/photonics/specialty-chemistry subsystems, plasma power supplies, ultra-high-purity subsystem manufacturing/cleaning, and critical gas/fluid delivery modules. These names are more cyclical and often customer-concentrated than the prime equipment OEMs, so the next diligence step is to verify exposure to leading-edge logic, HBM/advanced packaging, EUV-enabled process steps, order backlog, export-control sensitivity, and dependence on AMAT/LRCX/ASML/TSMC/Samsung/Intel capex timing. Expanded the universe for the leading-edge foundry/equipment node toward less-obvious second-order beneficiaries: advanced packaging/test capacity, metrology/inspection for HBM and chiplets, contamination-control materials, and critical subsystems used inside deposition/etch/lithography equipment.
